function_v0.doc:
Mirrors Blend's `submit(from, spender, to, requests) -> Positions`
ABI. Translates each request by DIRECTION:

- OUTBOUND (`Supply`, `SupplyCollateral`, `Repay`) on the
venue-wrapper asset: pre-wrap so the member holds the
wrapped balance the pool will debit.
- INBOUND (`Withdraw`, `WithdrawCollateral`, `Borrow`) on the
venue-wrapper asset: forward first, then unwrap what comes
back so the member holds the underlying.
- Types 6-9: refused with `Err::UnimplementedRequestType`.
Those are liquidator and auction paths, a different actor,
deliberately out of scope.

The returned `Positions` is the pool's response, passed through
unmodified.

### Unwrap amount

The facade measures the member's wrapped balance before doing
anything and again after the pool call, and unwraps the
increase. It does NOT unwrap `request.amount`, because Blend
independently caps all three inbound types and can refund an
outbound one:

- `Withdraw` / `WithdrawCollateral` are capped to the
member's actual position (`actions.rs:323`, `374`).
function_v0.name: submit

function_v0.doc:
View the wrapper's allowlist. Returns false for never-allowed
addresses.

THIS IS UX, NOT ENFORCEMENT. The wrapper's `transfer` gate is
the actual allowlist enforcement; a `false` return here means
`submit` will reject the call with `Err::NotAllowlisted`, not
that the address is barred from the underlying system.
function_v0.name: is_allowed

function_v0.doc:
Constructor. Runs ATOMICALLY with deploy, which is the only window in which pool and wrapped can be set. There is no separate `init` step and so no init front-run window for an attacker to claim these: the only way they are set is the deploy transaction itself. Requires `--pool

--wrapped ` at deploy time. There is no admin argument: see the file-level Immutability section.
function_v0.name: __constructor
